name: Exemption Medallions
reason: Source term 'Exemption Token' was renamed 'Exemption Medallion' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: Rare items in the Illusion Battlefield arc that let their holder avoid losing points when killed. Slade (source: Ming Dao) obtained three of them from a secret land, making him nearly impossible to punish by death in the arena.

name: Battle
reason: Generic common noun extracted from episode titles ('The Battle Of Life Force', 'Battle of Oracle City') and compound terms ('Stellar Battle Body'); not an entity.

name: Forsaken
reason: The source's 'Demi-Immortal Clan/Tribe' was renamed 'the Forsaken' for the Western fantasy setting; the episode's seven Spirit Supreme Realm warriors mirror the source's 'seven people of the Demi-Immortal Tribe' (ch 908).
description: The most powerful people among the Shadow Creatures of the void, holding absolute rule over them (Eps 931-932). In the source they correspond to the Demi-Immortal Clan, a neutral, incomparably powerful race formed from geniuses of many other races.

name: Soul Sealing Spell
reason: Source term 'Soul Sealing Technique' was localized as 'Soul Sealing Spell' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A dreaded binding art that seals a person's soul so they cannot control their own body, described as a fate worse than a forced marriage (Ep 927). In the source it is the technique that kept Feng Nianyun chained and sealed inside the crystal coffin.

name: Silverwood Pavilion
reason: Source organization 'Spring Fragrance Pavilion' was renamed 'Silverwood Pavilion' to fit the Western fantasy register; the episode lines about it claiming a talented woman after the tower trial mirror chapters 1060-1066 verbatim.
description: A powerful organization in the Thirteen Palaces region that recruits exceptionally talented women. After Layla's (source: Ai Anxin) performance in the tower trial, observers expected Silverwood Pavilion to claim her (Ep 1080).

name: Burns
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin surname. 'Burns' was chosen for the red-faced, taciturn guild chief; his source nickname 'Silent October/the silent one' became 'The Silent Man'.
description: Chief of the World Merchants' Guild Alliance (source: World Business Alliance), a Spirit-Tribulation Realm authority figure with a perpetually rosy complexion. A man of so few words that disciples call him 'The Silent Man'; he appears alongside Kieran and Hobbes during the Cloud Hall and tournament arcs (Eps 455-758).

name: Vincent
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xuan An' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Vincent'; the Ep 456 line 'Vincent, you go try it!' matches the source's 'Xuan An, you go and try it!' (ch 443).
description: A Black Mountain Sect warrior who tests the Rising Dragon Platform with a Dragon Jade Pendant at Raven's order and successfully ascends it (Ep 456).

name: Fleecy Downs
reason: The source location 'Hulun Grassland' was renamed 'Fleecy Downs' (pastoral grassland imagery) for the Western fantasy setting; Owen, the genius from Fleecy Downs, corresponds to Ao Xiang from the Hulun Grassland.
description: A grassland region thousands of miles from Oracle City, home of the saint-level genius Owen (source: Ao Xiang). Per the master sheet it is also where Owen discovered a treasure hoard left by an extinct order.

name: Celestial-level
reason: The source talent rank 'heaven-level' was localized as 'Celestial-level' to fit the Western fantasy register, per the show's master sheet.
description: A high tier in the martial-talent ranking system; sects scramble to recruit Celestial-level talents. Benson and several Ethereal Spirit Sect prodigies hold this rank (Eps 493-521).

name: Madness Trap
reason: Source term 'Chaos Trap' (the trap glyph Luo Zheng drew into Cloud Hall's defensive formation, ch 510) was localized as 'Madness Trap' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A trap Zane built into Cloud Hall's defenses and sealed into place against the enemy's assault (Eps 523-529); an ally lay in wait inside Cloud Hall for Zane's signal to spring it.

name: Poison King
reason: The literal source title 'Poison King' (of Wu Zhanhe) was retained unchanged in the adaptation.
description: The feared epithet of Simon (source: Wu Zhanhe), a poison master who in the source joined Cui Xie's Kingdom of Evil Deities. Bringing the so-called Poison King into the fold is described as a gamble (Eps 537-705).

name: Heavenly Eagle Prairie
reason: The literal source place name 'Heavenly Eagle Prairie' (ch 547) was retained unchanged in the adaptation.
description: A once-fertile grassland in the northeast corner of the continent where human, demon and other races long contested territory (Eps 562-684). After the demon forces weakened, the whole prairie became human pastureland.

name: Your Majesty
reason: Generic form of address used toward multiple different monarchs (War Emperor York, War King Wind, etc.); not an entity.

name: Goliath Bull-Toad
reason: The source creature 'Giant Mangku Toad' (the ferocious guardian of the western forbidden area, ch 620) was renamed 'Goliath Bull-Toad' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A monstrous toad dwelling in a forbidden area, so dangerous that Fabian dared not provoke it until he had no choice (Eps 639-661). In the source it swept away intruders of many races with its thick tongue.

name: Shadow-maws and Frost Wolves
reason: Compound conjunction of two separate creature types ('Shadow-maws' and 'Frost Wolves'), not a single entity; each creature type should be tracked on its own.

name: Elder Holt
reason: The character's Chinese surname 'Hu' (source 'Sect Elder Hu', ch 664) was localized to the similar-sounding Western surname 'Holt', keeping the 'Elder' title.
description: A ruthless sect elder in the Sea God Continent arc (Eps 684-687) who orders a stranded warrior killed regardless of resistance; Tessa confronts him over his actions. Corresponds to Sect Elder Hu of the Fish Dragon Sect episode in the source.

name: Dragon-Snare
reason: The source artifact 'Dragon-trapping Rope', the Void Spirit Sect's trump card left by Feng Guanyu (chs 680-681), was renamed 'Dragon-Snare' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: Arnold's legendary binding artifact, supposedly inescapable even for a warrior at the Life-and-Death Realm (Ep 700). In the source it is the Dragon-trapping Rope, used to bind Cui Xie with dragons of light so he could not circulate his energy.

name: Pyreton
reason: The source location 'Sunfire City' (also rendered 'Fiery Sun City', chs 688-690) was renamed 'Pyreton', preserving the fire imagery in a Western-style town name.
description: A mid-sized settlement, nothing like Ethereal City or Cloudhaven, populated mostly by ordinary folk after its strongest warriors marched off with their sects (Eps 708-709). A comet of violet fire landing near it opens the Violet-Core Physique arc.

name: Spirit Container
reason: The source artifact 'Spirit Goblet' (also 'Spirit Cup'), which the Heartless Master set up in the Northern Heaven Region and Luo Zheng destroyed (ch 717), was renamed 'Spirit Container'.
description: A sinister device Wallace (source: Heartless Master) set up in the Heartlands to harvest spirits; Zane destroyed it, drawing the villain's attention (Eps 738-808).

name: Violet Power Realm
reason: The source dimension 'Purple Extreme Realm' (also 'Extreme Purple Realm', chs 730-733) was renamed 'Violet Power Realm' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A separate dimension connected to the world by a spatial anchor, in which the sky is an endless field of giant suspended swords (Eps 753-756). In the source it is the realm tied to the Extreme Violet Yin Body, into which Xi Youqin pulls Luo Zheng.

name: Wisteria Martial House
reason: The source's 'Great Xuan Martial House', the leading Martial House of the Star Field Divine Kingdom (chs 777-780), was renamed 'Wisteria Martial House' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The premier martial academy of the Star Field Divine Kingdom, whose fighters compete in the inter-kingdom tournament (Eps 799-803). Its warriors cheer loudest for any champion of their kingdom, hoping for a victory over Logan (source: Yun Longtao).

name: War King
issues: Title drift: episodes alternate 'War Emperor' (e.g. War Emperor York, Ep 806) and 'War King' (e.g. War King Wind, Ep 818) for the source title 'War Emperor' held by several divine-kingdom monarchs; the 'War King' mentions in Eps 872-889 refer specifically to War King Wind (source: tianfeng war emperor), Fiona's father.
description: The royal title of the monarchs ruling the divine kingdoms (Eps 816-910), localizing the source's 'War Emperor'. In Eps 872-889 the War King in question is Fiona's father (source: Tianfeng War Emperor, Huo Yuner's father), who sizes up Zane as a prospective son-in-law and asks him directly whether he is married.

name: Heavenly Thunder Halberd
reason: The source weapon 'Heavenly Thunder Combat Halberd' (Liu Xiu's semi-divine weapon, ch 822) was shortened to 'Heavenly Thunder Halberd' in the adaptation.
description: A rune-covered halberd wielded by Fredrick (source: Liu Xiu), of nearly infinite value across the union of the seven divine kingdoms (Eps 845-908); it is ultimately lost along with its wielder's fortunes.

name: Purification Fire
reason: Source term 'Cleansing Fire' (Huo Yuner's purifying flame derived from the Law of Fire, ch 839) was localized as 'Purification Fire'.
description: A rare flame ability belonging to Fiona (source: Huo Yuner) with extraordinary purifying power, used to burn curse energy off cursed weapons; Zane realizes it can be used for far more than just curses (Eps 861-862).

name: Hank Shaw
reason: An adaptation-assigned name: the source leaves the Dragon Bloodline tomb corpses unnamed, so the adaptation named this vessel 'Hank Shaw' (a US-style name) when a soul takes it over.
description: A thin, withered old man's corpse kept in a coffin in the tomb arc and used as a possession vessel: a Soul Sea Realm master's soul merges with Hank's body and the reanimated corpse climbs out of its coffin (Ep 896). The possessed Hank later cuts his wrist and feeds golden blood into the Compass Wheel to escape the black wind blades (Ep 930).

name: Chantel
issues: Affiliation inconsistency: Ep 945 calls Chantel 'one of the Heavenly Feather Sanctuary's own masters' while Ep 946 calls her 'one of the Demon Night's Soul Sea Realm masters'; in the source Lady Lan Bing is a Divine Sea Realm expert of the Demon Night Clan (ch 920).
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Lan Bing' was fully localized to the US-origin feminine name 'Chantel'.
description: A Soul Sea Realm master of the Demon Night Clan (source: Lady Lan Bing) who intervenes in the battle at the Heavenly Feather Sanctuary, cutting off the enemy patriarch with her power and declaring herself his opponent (Eps 945-947).

name: Sacred Vault
reason: The source's 'Tianlu Bank' (the Zhang Family depository where Luo Zheng's crystals are held, ch 88) was renamed 'Sacred Vault' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A prestigious depository in The Capital where wealthy clients store crystals and valuables (Eps 102-105); its staff know that anyone bearing a gold medallion is either incredibly wealthy or dangerously influential.

name: Vitality Zane
reason: Extraction artifact: adjacency of the energy term 'Vitality' and the name 'Zane' across sentence boundaries; no contexts show it as a real entity.

name: Harpies
reason: The adaptation named the source's winged demon troops after the Western mythological harpy to give the demon army recognizable creature types.
description: Black, humanoid winged demons with scaly wings, primitive armor and longbows, serving as the air arm of the demon army that attacks Silverspire (Eps 125, 132); a group of them is sliced apart by shattered shield fragments.

name: High Smith
reason: The source's high rank of weapon-refining master was localized into Western smithing terminology as 'High Smith', consistent with the show's smith/cultivator vocabulary.
description: A high rank of weaponsmith in the adaptation's crafting hierarchy; Preston warns that Zane is more than just some High Smith (Eps 126-132).

name: Greene County
reason: The source location 'Guanghan County', the northernmost county of the Skyblaze Dynasty (chs 132-133), was renamed 'Greene County' as a Western-style county name.
description: A county the travelers pass through after the Sky Vault Forest (Eps 146-147); in the source it is the northernmost county of the Skyblaze Dynasty.

name: Pink Force Field
reason: One-off descriptive phrase for a barrier in a single scene (Ep 148), not a recurring named entity.

name: Wilson
issues: Name collision: the Soul Realm elder 'Wilson'/'Old Wilson' of Eps 151-153 (source: Old Huang / Elder Huang, chs 139-140) shares a surname with the later, unrelated ally Jacob Wilson (introduced ~Ep 253 per the master sheet); the two must not be merged.
reason: The character's Chinese surname 'Huang' was localized to the Western surname 'Wilson'; the Ep 151-153 group (long-haired woman, Old Wilson, Seymour) mirrors the source's long-haired woman, Elder Huang and Wanderer Wuyue.
description: An irascible old Soul Realm master (source: Old Huang / Elder Huang) among the experts exploring the Immortal Mansion (Eps 151-153). Openly hostile to Zane, he shrieks in disbelief when the younger man offers to attempt what the masters cannot.

name: Serene Void
reason: The source mental state 'Selfless Realm' (ch 146), which Luo Zheng comprehended while practicing the Soul-Shaking Thorn, was renamed 'the Serene Void' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A trance state of absolute detachment that Zane stumbled into while mastering the Psyche Spike: his consciousness retreats into a 'Sphere of Nothingness' and observes his body from afar, untouched by sensation or suffering. He uses it to endure the Soul Test on the steps (Ep 160) and the agony of the dragon-scale transformation (Eps 866-876), though extreme pain can knock him out of it.
